title: Check yourself: Delegating and describing a task

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A team lead wants an assistant to prepare a weekly status email from a spreadsheet of task progress notes. The email goes to executives. Which division of work is soundest?

options.text: Claude writes the first version; a person verifies facts and approves sending
options.says: Drafting is language-shaped and reviewable, while checking facts and approving the send stay with a person (the worked example's table).

options.text: A person writes the email; Claude only corrects spelling and grammar
options.says: Ruled out because Claude "saves the time spent on prose", the main saving, which a person writing everything forgoes.

options.text: Claude drafts and also decides which blockers to escalate to executives
options.says: Ruled out because escalation is "judgment that carries accountability", which stays with a person.

options.text: Claude collects the notes, writes the email and sends it, with spot checks later
options.says: Ruled out because the table keeps "Check every figure in the draft against the source" with a person or a script, and spot checks later come after readers have the email.

origin.section: Delegate: which steps go to Claude

questions.stem: Someone asks Claude: "Summarise this report." The result is accurate, but the sales team who asked cannot use it. Which gap in the request most likely caused this?

options.text: It lacked a role line naming Claude an expert summariser
options.says: Ruled out because a role line names no reader or purpose, and the page says to "Add what a colleague new to the job would need".

options.text: It omitted a word limit, which is why the summary missed the sales angle
options.says: Ruled out because without the goal "Claude cannot choose between reasonable readings", and a limit is only a constraint on form.

options.text: It never said who would read it or what they must decide with it
options.says: The description should cover the goal and the context, who reads it and why, and a generic request gets a generic reply.

options.text: It ran on a tier too small to judge what matters to sales
options.says: Ruled out because "the description is where most of the quality is decided", and a larger tier does not know the readers either.
